beats: Hook: can you find out whether two qubits are equal without finding out what either of them is? A staircase light wired to two hidden switches lights when they agree: you learn agree or disagree, never which way either switch is (line_qc_parity_hall_bulb, then the cover).

The blunt way (Q25-07 23:39-28:26, s22): ZZ as two separate Z measurements: four outcomes, both values learnt. Harmless for a plain 00 or 11, but for an entangled pair (|00>+|11>)/sqrt2 it destroys the very superposition you wanted to keep (Q24-08 36:36-37:17) (line_qc_parity_open_flaps: lifting both flaps; reuse line_qc_meas_flick_or_slap for 'reading ends it').
XX: turn both qubits first with Hadamards, then the same Z readings (27:23-28:22; reuse line_qc_meas_fixed_camera).

The four Bell states form a basis (28:28-33:17); the Bell circuit (H, then CNOT) is the pairing machine: two plain inputs in, one of four matched pairs out (line_qc_pair_machine). Honest caveat: matching cups stand for matching Z readings only; a real Bell pair also matches when both halves are read the X way, which no pair of dice does (QC04-04).

Bell measurement = the Bell circuit run backwards, then two Z readings: two lamps, two bits, which of the four pairs it was (33:17-38:56, Q24-08 40:30-46:22; clip Q25-07 34:03-34:29 'like a hello world program'; line_qc_pair_machine_reverse; tape Q25-07 s34).

Measuring any +-1 operator U with one helper (38:56-49:35): the helper starts at 0, then H, controlled-U, H, and only the helper is read: 0 means eigenvalue +1, 1 means -1; the data qubits are never read (clips 42:03-42:32 and 49:05-49:33; line_qc_parity_wall_wiring: the bulb is the helper, wired to both switches).

With U = ZZ that is the agree / disagree question; a pair in (|00>+|11>)/sqrt2 answers 'agree' and stays exactly as it was: the quantum payoff a light switch cannot show (back to line_qc_parity_hall_bulb).

Partial measurement (Q24-08 46:40-52:27, Q24-08.notes p4): read one qubit of a Bell pair and the other's Z reading is settled too, yet its holder sees nothing change: no message travels (line_qc_parity_far_cups; full story in QC04-04). Avoid Q24-08 43:04 (a student's answer).

Plant for QC08-02: three hidden switches and two bulbs between neighbours; a lit bulb points at the odd switch without anyone reading a switch: this circuit becomes the syndrome measurement (line_qc_parity_three_switches).
Cover (line_qc_cover_06_02; for the X post and thumbnails, not a film beat): the staircase, two hidden switches, one lit bulb, the experimenter looking up at it, pleased.

drawings.name: line_qc_parity_hall_bulb
drawings.prompt: Inside a plain house, a straight staircase seen from the side, rising from the lower left to the upper right, with a simple handrail. On the wall at the foot of the stairs and on the wall at the top of the stairs is one wall plate each, and each wall plate is covered by a small closed hinged flap, so the switch under it cannot be seen. Halfway up, one bare light bulb hangs from the ceiling on a short cord; it is lit (an empty bulb outline with short straight rays around it). The experimenter (an invented young adult with a simple round face and dot eyes, short spiky hair, safety goggles pushed up on the forehead, a white lab coat with the sleeves rolled up over a plain T-shirt, and sneakers) stands at the foot of the stairs, looking up at the bulb with one finger raised, pleased, as if something has just become clear. Portrait image 1024x1536; the staircase, the bulb and the character fill about 85% of the width and about 88% of the height. No text, no letters, no numbers, no logos, no pictures on the walls.
